problem: Roth's theorem in [N]: how large can a 3AP-free subset of {1,...,N} be?
board: Density increment with Bohr sets -- the board Kelley-Meka 2023 ran on, and the board Bloom-Sisask re-present with classical Bohr set machinery.

ceiling.quantity: the exponent e in |A| <= exp(-c (log N)^e) N; larger e is a stronger upper bound
ceiling.cap_scope: ANY argument that uses any sort of density-increment argument with Bohr sets, whether using Kelley-Meka ideas or a more traditional Fourier analytic approach -- the authors' own words, so the cap is on the BOARD, not on their argument

truth.what_establishes_it: Behrend 1946 constructs 3AP-free subsets of [N] of size at least exp(-c (log N)^{1/2}) N, with small improvements by Elkin 2011 and Green-Wolf 2010. So no upper bound with exponent above 1/2 can exist, and the truth is at exponent 1/2 or below it.

quote: Of course, the Behrend exponent of 1/2 would be the final target, but this seems quite far out of reach still; indeed, an exponent of 1/3 (or perhaps even 1/4) seems to be the limit of any argument that uses any sort of 'density increment' argument with Bohr sets (whether using Kelley-Meka ideas or a more traditional Fourier analytic approach).
source: arXiv:2302.07211v3 (Bloom, Sisask, 'The Kelley-Meka bounds for sets free of three-term arithmetic progressions'), 'Improvements' paragraph
source_as_of: 2025-05-13 (v3); the same paragraph also announces 1/9 and 5/41 as improvements on Theorem 1's 1/12

state_of_the_board_when_registered.announced_by_the_same_paper: 1/9 with a clean modification, 5/41 after technical optimisation
state_of_the_board_when_registered.so_the_gap_to_the_cap: even the believed natural limit 1/7 = 0.1429 is well short of the stated board cap 1/3 = 0.3333, which is itself short of the truth at 1/2

resolution_criterion: RESOLVES AS broken-on-the-same-board if an upper bound with exponent strictly above 1/3 is proved by a density-increment-with-Bohr-sets argument. RESOLVES AS held-and-board-left if an exponent above 1/3 is proved by an argument that is not of that kind, or if the authors' cap is superseded by a stated cap from the same board. Improvements at or below 1/3 that stay on the board (1/9, 5/41, 1/7, anything up to 1/3) resolve NOTHING: they are the cap being approached, which is what the statement predicts.

prediction.claim: The exponent will not pass 1/3 by a density-increment-with-Bohr-sets argument. If it passes 1/3 at all, it will be by leaving that board.
prediction.by: this session, sealed before any resolution exists
prediction.confidence: this is the AUTHORS' prediction, adopted rather than formed independently -- it is registered to test the REGISTER, not to display judgement of mine
prediction.horizon: unknown and probably long. Stated plainly: an item that may not resolve for a decade cannot validate a benchmark on this project's timescale. The register's value is that the label is not hindsight, not that it is fast.

problem: Bounded prime gaps: are there infinitely many n with p_{n+1} - p_n bounded?
board: The GPY one-dimensional Selberg sieve -- weights lambda_d built from a single-variable F, with the criterion (1/2)*theta*rho_k(F) > 1, where theta is the level of distribution supplied from outside the sieve.

ceiling.quantity: rho_k(F) = [k/(k+2l+1)] * [2(2l+1)/(l+1)] for the one-variable F = (1-x)^l used in GPY, which the criterion needs to be large
ceiling.boundary_note: rho_k(F) increases in both factors but is bounded by 4 and NEVER REACHES IT, for any k: sup over one-variable F at k = 10^9 is 3.9990. The board can reach every value below 4 and no value at or above it. Granville's Proposition 6.3 needs rho(F) > 4h unconditionally (h = 1) and > 2h under Elliott-Halberstam, so under Bombieri-Vinogradov's theta = 1/2 the criterion's value caps at 2*theta = 1 while it must EXCEED 1. The board misses by an epsilon that no k closes, which is why the cap and the requirement are the same number.
ceiling.cap_scope: every one-variable F, every k -- the saturation is independent of k, which is the load-bearing clause
ceiling.derivation: p1-retrodiction/tools/check_citations_response.py section (d), which tabulates rho(k,l) against the citations response's own figures and computes the supremum

truth.what_establishes_it: In 2005 bounded gaps was believed, not proved -- the twin prime conjecture and its relatives. So this cap is a cap relative to a CONJECTURED truth, and must be read as one. That is the register's second tier distinction and this instance is why it exists: unlike Behrend's construction in the Roth entry, nothing here proved the target was reachable.

quote: Proposition 6.3 gives rho(F) > 4h unconditionally, > 2h under Elliott-Halberstam; and the before-board reads 'theta > 1/2 needed; BV gives exactly 1/2'. The REQUIREMENT is stated by the source; the CAP -- that no one-variable F reaches it for any k -- is derived here and checked in code, not quoted.
source: Granville, 'Primes in intervals of bounded length', arXiv:1410.8400, sections 5 and 6 (Proposition 6.3), via the citations response transcript; cap computed in check_citations_response.py section (d)
source_as_of: 2014 exposition of the 2005 GPY board; the requirement theta > 1/2 was known to GPY themselves at the time
resolution_criterion: Resolved by history: did anyone get bounded gaps from a one-variable F under theta = 1/2?

what_happened.outcome: The cap held. The advance came TWICE, and both times by leaving a board -- which is the register's first confirmation that a stated-or-derived ceiling is worth encoding.
what_happened.maynard_tao_2013: Left the sieve board. A multidimensional sieve makes the ratio grow like log k rather than saturating: log k - 2 log log k - 1 is about 0.55 at k = 105 and about 7.6 at k = 10^6, against the one-variable cap of 4. This is case 7a, the positive.
what_happened.zhang_2013: Did NOT leave the sieve board. He raised theta past 1/2 for smooth moduli -- Theorem 3.2, Q = x^{1/2+eta}, delta = 1/1168 -- by changing the EQUIDISTRIBUTION board one level down. This is control 16, and it is why debt D30 exists: the level has to be stated or the control is mislabelled.
what_happened.the_lesson_for_the_register: A ceiling names WHICH board is capped, and an advance can come from leaving a DIFFERENT board than the one the cap is stated about. Zhang beat the theta > 1/2 requirement without touching the capped sieve. So a ceiling's resolution must record the LEVEL at which the board changed, not just whether one did.

diagnostic_reading.product_law_matching: Fires on case 7a (the positive) and correctly does not fire on control 16 -- but note that this is scored in the retrospective arm, so D25 applies: a rater who recognises 'bounded prime gaps, 2013' needs no rule.
diagnostic_reading.bound_strength_test_D28: The cap here is on a CRITERION, not on a bound against a construction, so the one-line bound-strength test has nothing to read. The Roth entry is the reverse. Two instances, two different readings -- neither test covers both.
